MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 23, 2023
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:00 p.m., on May 23, 2023, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 18, 2023, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (left meeting at 8:25 pm)
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  Council Member Ruesch

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

 CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Threat to Public Services or Facilities: Consultation with Orange County
  Sheriff's Department; Captain McDonald and Orange County Intelligence
  Analysis Center (OCIAC) Director Martinez

 CS2.  Liability Claims and Existing Litigation: Claimant: Villanea GAL Castillo,
  Heirs of Wolf, Heirs of Oldmixon and Loos-Hannifan: Agency Claimed
  Against – City of Mission Viejo and: Significant Exposure to Litigation
  Pursuant to Paragraph (2) of Subdivision (d) Section 54956.9 (4 cases)

City Council Minutes  1  May 23, 2023
  RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

 At the hour of 5:01 pm, Mayor Goodell recessed to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened
 at 6:06 pm with four City Council Members present and Council Member Ruesch absent.

 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

 City Attorney Bill Curley stated there were two closed session items but no action was taken.

 INVOCATION: Rabbi Marcus of the Chabad Jewish Center

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

 PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Proclaim the Month of May to Be Jewish American Heritage Month

  Mayor Goodell presented proclamation to Rabbi Marcus of the Chabad Jewish Center.

 P2.  Proclaim June 2, 2023 To Be National Gun Violence Awareness Day

  Mayor Goodell presented proclamation to Bita Karabian ~ OC Moms Demand Action
  Volunteer.

 PUBLIC COMMENTS

 William Palma, M.V.: Spoke on racism, hate speech, harassment and in particular an incident
 at his home. He referred to emails and a handout he shared with the Council pertaining to a
 lawsuit against the City.

 Kim Carr.: Stated she represented Senator Blakespear, and thanked the City Council for
 acknowledging June 2, as National Gun Violence Awareness Day. She added that the Senator
 shares the same commitment to preventing gun violence and has introduced two Bills SB417
 and SB452. Lastly, she encouraged residents to contact the Senator https://sd38.senate.ca.gov/
 on any legislative matter, not just gun violence.

 James Farris, M.V.: Voiced his concerns related to crime, and the improper actions of the
 OCSD and staff of Mission Viejo. He referred to the handout he provided the City Council
 outlining many problems in the City, and concluded by stating this woke mentality needs to
 stop.

 Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Suggested the Council invite Michael Block to a future Council Meeting
 as he put the City of Mission Viejo on the map this past weekend with a hole in one at the PGA
 Championships. He added that the Core Area Vision Plan should be item P3, and not item #25
 on the agenda, and lastly with regards to item #19, he hopes the City has funds set aside to
 cover attorney fees incurred by Michael Schlesinger.

City Council Minutes  2  May 23, 2023
  Rita Tayenaka, M.V.: Gave kudos to the City Council for everything that they do. She stated
 that this is a wonderful City to represent as a realtor, and appreciates all that the City offers.

 Lezlie Trujillo, M.V.: Asked for the City’s assistance/support with regards to residents living
 next to someone who smokes marijuana, and also asked for help with Waste Management and
 the additional organics waste recycling trash can, required by the City.

 Victoria Bruno, M.V.: Spoke on the management of open spaces, in particular the 9 acres of
 open space on Jeronimo north of Oso Creek. She shared her concerns and ideas in conserving
 native plants, storm water management, and practicing proactive weed abatement to help
 preserve open spaces.

 Walt Lawson, M.V.: Commended the City Council for the presentation proclaiming June 2, as
 National Gun Violence Awareness Day. He stated numerous actions that need to be taken in
 order to reduce gun violence/deaths in the US. Lastly, he asked the Council to sponsor a
 program to discuss gun violence, and prepare a Council Resolution to be forwarded onto the
 Legislator.

 Tom Moore, M.V.: Commented on the handout/photograph he provided to the City Council
 of the South East corner of Marguerite and La Paz Road and asked for sign to be removed.

 Linda Shepard, M.V.: Requested the City Council stand against AB665 Minors: consent to
 mental health services, and SB107 providing refuge for trans kids and their families. She also
 commented on the Core Area Vision Plan, had a number of questions, and stated she is unsure
 if she supports this plan, like she did NPM, and the Golf Course as there are a lot of pros and
 cons.

 Eric Cernich, Newport Beach: Stated his family owns Trader Joe’s and commented on the
 upcoming Core Area Vision Plan Presentation. He also mentioned that he is interested in
 forming a public/private partnership with the City in order to redevelop the center. Lastly, he
 raised questions pertaining to parking/deliveries, the zoning of the center to a park, and the
 CC&R’s.

 Carols Pianelli, M.V.: Spoke in support of the Core Area Vision Plan and potential playhouse
 theatre. He also referenced the handout he provided to the City Council pertaining to the
 restoration of the Garden Plaza and the overwhelming response of residents in favor of the
 restoration.

 Don Newton, M.V.: Voiced his concerns on the dangers of Oso Parkway between Felipe and
 Marguerite, and questioned why there is zero policing in that section of the road.

 Jann Kronick, Long Beach: Stated she is the owner of the Michaels Building and addressed the
 Core Area Vison Plan. She commented on the breach of the CC&R’s, the owners’ rights being
 ignored, parking/deliveries issues and the lack of consideration of the tenants.

 Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Criticized the City Attorney, the City Manager, the Assistant City
 Manager, and the City Council. She spoke of her concerns on the Core Area Vision Plan, the
City Council Minutes  3  May 23, 2023
  related costs, and the City’s violation of the CC&R’s. She commented on the lack of
 transparency with regards to Larry Ryan not being identified as a paid consultant on this project.
 Lastly, she asked the City to add a comments section to the website so that residents may voice
 their opinion on the Core Area Vision Plan.

 Council Members asked various questions of staff and the City Attorney.

  (1) Awarded contract (A23-20) for subject services to Real Estate Consulting and

City Council Minutes  5  May 23, 2023
   amount not to exceed $80,000.00, pending adoption of the Fiscal Year 2023-2025 budget

  (1) Awarded contract (A23-22) for the subject services to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the

  authorized issuance of a purchase order for Landscape Contract Area 9 to Nieves

 NEW BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  6  May 23, 2023
  19.  Establish General Fund Target and Minimum Reserve Levels for 2023-25 Budget

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to

  CITY MANAGER REPORT (Item taken out of order)

  25.  Core Area Vision Plan Presentation and Summary of Public Input

  Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay and Assistant Engineer Mario Gutierrez
  presented the staff report.

  Bryan Zahn, M.V.: Spoke in favor of the Core Area Vision Plan and the process required
  for this vision to come to fruition. He added, this project is a need and not a want, and
  stated that he has been approached by numerous residents asking him ~ when. Lastly,
  he asked the Council to support this project, think about recreation and much needed
  dining, plus the resident’s needs.

City Council Minutes  7  May 23, 2023
   Walt Lawson, M.V.: Recapped the public comments he made at the May 9, and April
  25, Council Meeting pertaining to cost, timeline, Santa Margarita Water District,
  CC&R’s, parking and communication with property owners of the Core Area Vision
  Plan.

  Cathy Palmer, M.V.: Stated there are aspects of plan that she supports, and gave
  examples. She added that the plan would get her full support if it was privately financed
  with mixed use housing, and asked the Council to revisit the benefits of a private/public
  partnership. She concluded by stating some of her concern; costs, CC&R’s, parking and
  how this Vision Plan ties in with the existing properties.

  Tom Moore, M.V.: Spoke in favor of the Core Area Vision Plan, however, he added
  there is a lack of participation with the other property owners. He requested the City
  develop a specific plan of the area, not only the commercially zoned but also include the
  surroundings residential properties. Lastly, he stated Keith is doing a tremendous job,
  and the City is seeking input, so he encouraged residents to participate and be patient as
  this project will take a number of years.

  Dwayne Ihde, M.V.: Spoke in support of the Core Area Vision Plan and encouraged
  others to do likewise. He stated young families, like himself, are the future of Mission
  Viejo and will continue to invest in the City. He added the City needs a downtown for
  families and friends to enjoy, and this Vision Plan encourages residents to stay in
  Mission Viejo and not leave to neighboring cities.

  Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Referred to the handout he provided the City Council listing
  questions pertaining to costs, private funding, approval of existing businesses, shared
  expenses, referendum, and the needs of Mission Viejo residents. He concluded by
  stating the Council should be able to tell residents how much has been spent to date.

  Ilene Geiger, M.V.: Stated although the Core Area Vision Plan is lovely, she voiced her
  concerns related to costs, services that will be cut to cover such costs, housing crisis,
  gap funding, benefit of proposed plan, etc. She requested a more realistic video showing
  the entire strip mall including those properties without upgrades, and asked the Council
  to consider the cost benefit analysis of the project.

  Larry Ryan, M.V.: Stated that former speaker Dwayne Ihde is the essence of what this
  project is all about, having pride in the community and wanting something for
  everybody. He also thanked Cathy Schlicht for the shout out. He added, that he spent
  the better part of his life in Mission Viejo and this project is a vision for tomorrow, a
  look into the future. Lastly, he referred to the City of Lake Forest having a vision e.g.
  Lake Forest Sports Park long before they owned the property, how the details were
  worth perusing, and he hopes the Council will support this project.

  Mindy Geller, M.V.: Stated she is the owner of “The Patio” at the entrance of the
  privately-owned shopping center, apart from the SteinMart building purchased by the
  City. She mentioned the City is making changes which are in violation of CC&R’s.
  Voiced her concerns related to parking, traffic reports, and safety issues, and offered to
City Council Minutes  8  May 23, 2023
   meet with the City to review this. Added the City will prevent business from operating
  if they go ahead with this Vision Plan. She stated that the City Council and Staff have
  repeated said they would work with the owners of plaza, yet this has not happened.
  Spoke of rising cost of materials, money owed to Property Manager Kathy Sickles,
  SDGE fees, and the need for an environmental study. How employees and paid
  consultants should be allowed to speak on this project, and lastly, she questioned why
  no budget or expenses have been shared with owners and residents ~ what does the City
  have to hide.

  Wade Weiman, Rolling Hills: Co-owner of “The Patio”. Voiced the same concerns as
  Jann, Eric and Mindy with regards to CC&R’s, access ways, reduction in parking,
  accessibility, tenants paying double taxes, SDGE fees, etc. He addressed City Attorney
  Bill Curley’s comment that the contract has been approved by Kathy Sickles, yet in fact
  she is revising changes to the contract. Questioned the fees, and added that Randy Leff
  now represents the parcel owners, who are trying to work together to form a committee
  and work with the City. Lastly, he asked for transparency, and for everyone to work
  together in order to move forward.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg outlined the facts of the matter. He stated the reason the
  City reached out to Mr. Leff earlier this afternoon was in anticipation of the same drama
  from the property owners, that being, that the City is not working with the property
  owners. He referenced the minutes from the February 24, 2023, meeting, three months
  ago. At that time, a committee was formed identifying which property owners would
  serve on the committee and begin working on the Property Management Agreement,
  Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws and amendments to the CC& R’s. Wade Weiman &
  Kathy Sickles were to facilitate that next meeting. Three months later, the City has
  heard nothing. Hence, the City Attorney was tasked with drafting the Property
  Management Agreement that was provided to Ms. Sickles for her review. City Manager
  Wilberg concluded, that the City has been patient, however, the City cannot simply pay
  CAM charges without a contract.

  City Attorney Bill Curley added that Attorney Randy Leff stated this afternoon, that Jann
  Kronick is his only client. He referenced a series of emails to Ms. Sickles pertaining to
  the contract which he amended and sent with Mr. Leff. Seeing as he heard nothing further
  from Ms. Sickles, he was unaware of any problems mentioned this evening. He reviewed
  the same four step process with Mr. Leff. The need to get a Management Agreement in
  place so that CAM charges can be paid, and electric can be split, followed by the Articles
  of Incorporation, the Bylaws and amending the CC&R’s. He added, all this has been
  talked about for months and documented. The City is more than ready and trying to work
  with the property owners. He concurred that the CC&R’s are defective, incomplete, with
  no management organization, which is why Mr. Leff, Ms. Kronick and Mr. Cernich
  approached the City last June with a need to update CC&R’s. The City agreed and has
  been trying to move forward, yet all they get is resistance from the property owners.
  Lastly, City Attorney Bill Curley stated that the CC&R’s preclude residential housing.

 26.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

 Council Member Vasquez

 Council Member Vasquez had no additional comments.

 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

 Mayor Pro Tem Kelley reminded everyone that the City is holding a Memorial Day Ceremony
 on Monday, May 29 at 8:30am. She announced that she attended the Opioid Crisis event, all
 three OCSD bicycle events, a Hazing event at NPM, the Sierra Open House and Water Safety
 Day, Symphony-on-the-Go at Pavion Park, and the South Orange County Economic Coalition
 Health Services Presentation this morning with the Mayor Goodell. A very busy couple of
 weeks. She also shared that she missed the Medal of Valor Ceremony on May 4, and felt it
 important that we recognize the five OSCD Heros. Deputy Dombrowski who received a medal
 for life saving, Deputy Cole who received a medal for courage, Deputy Sanchez, Deputy DeCaro
 and Sergeant Anderson who also received a medal for life saving.

 Mayor Goodell

 Mayor Goodell had no additional comments.

City Council Minutes  10  May 23, 2023
